title: Probability: Chance from 0 to 1
seo_title: Probability – Primary 6 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Describe the chance of events using words and numbers from 0 to 1; find the probability of simple events. (summary of the NERDC Primary 6 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 6 maths worksheets on probability: impossible, unlikely, even chance, likely and certain, probabilities as fractions and simple events with dice, coins and bags. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Probability tells us how likely something is. Impossible = 0, certain = 1, even chance = 1/2.
  • Probability of an event = number of favourable outcomes ÷ total number of outcomes.
  • The probability that something does not happen = 1 − the probability that it happens.

Examples

Example

A die shows an even number

2, 4, 6 out of 6

Answer: 3/6 = 1/2

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Giving a probability bigger than 1Probabilities are between 0 and 1.
Counting outcomes twiceList the outcomes carefully.
Thinking unlikely means impossibleUnlikely events can still happen.

faq.q: What is the probability of a coin landing heads?

faq.a: Yes, if the event is impossible.

items.q: The sun will rise tomorrow morning. This is …
items.e: The sun rises every morning. It always happens, so it is certain.

items.q: After Wednesday, the next day will be Thursday. This is …
items.e: The days of the week always come in the same order. Thursday always comes after Wednesday, so it is certain.

items.q: Kelechi is 8. Next year he will be 9. This is …
items.e: Everyone is one year older each year. 8 + 1 = 9, so it is certain.

items.q: Tomorrow will have 30 hours. This is …
items.e: Every day has 24 hours. A day can never have 30 hours, so it is impossible.

items.q: If Amaka drops a tennis ball, it will fall down. This is …
items.e: When you let go of a ball, it always falls to the ground. It must happen, so it is certain.

items.q: Yusuf is 8. Next year he will be 3 years old. This is …
items.e: You cannot get younger. Next year Yusuf will be 9, so being 3 is impossible.

items.q: The next vehicle that drives past the school will have 4 wheels. This is …
items.e: Most vehicles on the road are cars with 4 wheels. But the next one could be a motorbike or a truck, so it is likely, not certain.

items.q: Joy will drink some water at school today. This is …
items.e: Most pupils drink water during a school day. Joy could forget, so it is likely, not certain.

items.q: Dayo will roll a 6 on a dice five times in a row. This is …
items.e: Rolling a 6 once is unlikely (1 out of 6 faces). Five 6s in a row is even harder. It could happen, so it is unlikely, not impossible.

items.q: Which event is certain?
c: Ngozi will win her race at the inter-house sports
Kayode will have spaghetti for dinner
items.e: Friday always comes after Thursday, so it is certain. Rain, winning a race and spaghetti for dinner might happen, but they might not.

items.q: Which event is impossible?
c: A cat will fly to the Moon
It will be sunny on Saturday
Zainab will lose a tooth this year
Samuel will see a bird today
items.e: A cat cannot fly, and it cannot get to the Moon, so this can never happen. The other events could happen.

items.q: Which event is unlikely?
c: Pupils will eat lunch at school today
A fish will ride a bike
A snake will be found in the school library
items.e: A snake in the library could happen, but it is rare, so it is unlikely. The sun setting is certain, a fish riding a bike is impossible, and pupils eating lunch is likely.

items.q: How likely is this? It will rain in Kano in July.
items.e: Likely.

items.q: How likely is this? The sun will rise in the east tomorrow.
items.e: Certain.

items.q: How likely is this? A goat will fly to school.
items.e: Impossible.

items.q: How likely is this? You will roll a 7 on a normal dice.
items.e: Impossible.

items.q: How likely is this? You will roll an even number on a dice.
items.e: Equally likely.

items.q: How likely is this? You will pick a red ball from a bag of only blue balls.
items.e: Impossible.

items.q: How likely is this? A tossed coin will land on heads.
items.e: Equally likely.

items.q: How likely is this? You will pick a blue ball from a bag with 9 red balls and 1 blue ball.
items.e: Unlikely.

items.q: The spinner has 4 equal sections. Which colour is the arrow most likely to land on?
c: red and blue are equally likely
items.e: 3 of the 4 equal sections are red and only 1 is blue, so red is most likely. (There is no green, so green is impossible.)

items.q: The spinner has 6 equal sections. Which colour is the arrow least likely to land on?
items.e: Only 1 of the 6 equal sections is green. 5 are yellow. Green has the smallest part, so it is least likely.

items.q: Landing on red is …
items.e: Every section is red. The arrow must land on red, so it is certain.

items.q: Landing on red is …
items.e: Only 1 of the 6 equal sections is red. It can happen, but not often, so it is unlikely. It is not impossible, because there is a red section.

items.q: Landing on green is …
items.e: There is no green section on this spinner. The arrow can never land on green, so it is impossible.

items.q: Landing on green is …
items.e: 5 of the 6 equal sections are green, so green is likely. It is not certain, because there is 1 purple section.

items.q: Which colour can the arrow never land on?
items.e: The spinner has red, blue and yellow sections only. There is no green, so landing on green is impossible.

items.q: Which colour is the arrow most likely to land on?
c: all three colours are equally likely
items.e: Look at the size of each part, not the number of sections. Blue is one big section: half of the spinner. Red is 2 small sections (a quarter) and yellow is 2 small sections (a quarter). So blue is most likely.

items.q: Which two colours are equally likely?
items.e: Red and green are each a quarter of the spinner. Parts of the same size are equally likely. Yellow is half of the spinner, so it is more likely than red or green.

items.q: Landing on yellow is …
items.e: Yellow is only a quarter of the spinner and green is three quarters. Yellow can happen, but it is unlikely.

items.q: Zainab picks one counter from the bag without looking. Which colour is she most likely to pick?
c: red and blue are equally likely
items.e: There are 6 red counters and only 2 blue counters. More red counters means red is more likely.

items.q: Victor picks one counter without looking. Which colour is he least likely to pick?
items.e: There is only 1 green counter and 7 yellow counters, so green is least likely.

items.q: Picking a blue counter from this bag is …
items.e: Every counter in the bag is blue, so you must pick blue. It is certain.

items.q: Picking a green counter from this bag is …
items.e: There are only red and yellow counters. There is no green counter, so it is impossible.

items.q: Picking a red counter from this bag is …
items.e: 7 of the 8 counters are red, so red is likely. It is not certain, because there is 1 blue counter.

items.q: Picking a red counter from this bag is …
items.e: Only 1 of the 10 counters is red. It can happen, but not often, so it is unlikely, not impossible.

items.q: Which colour is impossible to pick from this bag?
items.e: The bag has red, blue and yellow counters. There is no green, so green is impossible. There is 1 yellow counter, so yellow is unlikely, not impossible.

items.q: Which sentence is true?
c: Red and blue are equally likely
Red is more likely than blue
items.e: There are 4 red and 4 blue counters. The same number of each colour means they are equally likely.

items.q: This bag has 9 green marbles and 1 purple marble. Bisi picks one marble without looking. Picking the purple marble is …
items.e: Only 1 of the 10 marbles is purple. It can happen, but it is unlikely.

items.q: Which two colours are equally likely to be picked?
items.e: There are 3 red, 3 blue and 2 yellow counters. Red and blue have the same number, so they are equally likely.

items.q: A bag has 5 blue, 5 white and 6 red counters. One counter is taken at random. What is the probability it is blue?
items.e: There are 16 counters and 5 are blue: P(blue) = 516.

items.q: A fair six-sided dice is rolled. What is the probability of getting a number less than 3?
items.e: 2 of the 6 outcomes work, so P = 26 = 13.

items.q: A fair six-sided dice is rolled. What is the probability of getting a factor of 6?
items.e: 4 of the 6 outcomes work, so P = 46 = 23.

items.q: A card is picked at random from a normal pack of 52 cards. What is the probability it is a picture card (jack, queen or king)?
items.e: There are 12 such cards out of 52: 1252 = 313.

items.q: A fair spinner has 8 equal sections. 7 of them are blue. What is the probability of landing on blue?
items.e: 7 out of 8 equal sections: 78.

items.e: There are 15 counters and 3 are white: P(white) = 315 = 15.

items.q: A bag has 5 red, 6 yellow and 2 white counters. One counter is taken at random. What is the probability it is white?
items.e: There are 13 counters and 2 are white: P(white) = 213.

items.q: A card is picked at random from a normal pack of 52 cards. What is the probability it is a heart?
items.e: There are 13 such cards out of 52: 1352 = 14.

items.q: A bag has 5 yellow, 8 green and 5 blue counters. One counter is taken at random. What is the probability it is yellow?

items.q: A card is picked at random from a normal pack of 52 cards. What is the probability it is a king?
items.e: There are 4 such cards out of 52: 452 = 113.

items.q: A bag has 7 green, 8 red and 2 blue counters. One counter is taken at random. What is the probability it is green?
items.e: There are 17 counters and 7 are green: P(green) = 717.

items.q: A bag has 4 white, 9 green and 7 red counters. One counter is taken at random. What is the probability it is white?
items.e: There are 20 counters and 4 are white: P(white) = 420 = 15.

items.q: A fair six-sided dice is rolled. What is the probability of getting a 3?
items.e: 1 of the 6 outcomes work, so P = 16.

items.q: A fair spinner has 8 equal sections. 7 of them are red. What is the probability of landing on red?
items.e: 7 out of 8 equal sections: 78.

items.q: A fair six-sided dice is rolled. What is the probability of getting a prime number?
items.e: 3 of the 6 outcomes work, so P = 36 = 12.

items.q: A fair spinner has 5 equal sections. 3 of them are red. What is the probability of landing on red?
items.e: 3 out of 5 equal sections: 35.

items.q: A spinner can land on red, blue or green. P(red) = 0.2 and P(blue) = 0.1. What is P(green)?
items.e: All the probabilities add up to 1: 1 − 0.2 − 0.1 = 0.7.

items.q: The probability that it rains tomorrow is 0.9. What is the probability that it does not rain?
